newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's future leader says worth $47.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's future leader says worth $47.5 million.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has a US$47.5 million stake in his family shipping firm, his office said on Friday in a statement intended to show transparency and boost confidence in the incoming government.
The figure is based on Tung's ownership of 80,835,548 non-voting shares representing 15.6 percent of Oriental Overseas (International) Ltd.
Tung will replace British colonial Governor Chris Patten as Hong Kong's leader when the territory reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Oriental Overseas, a publicly listed company, is capitalised at US$304 million at current market prices. Shares in the group ended on Friday at HK$4.55 (58 U.S. cents).
However, Tung said he owned nothing more than the stake in his family business, not even property.

His wife, Betty, was the sole beneficial shareholder of a company which owns their two apartments in Hong Kong, while his villa in the prestigious Deep Water Bay district of Hong Kong belonged to his family trust, he said in the statement.
Tung also said there were three apartments in the United States -- in New York City, San Francisco and Salt Lake City -- which were owned by a trust for the benefit of his children.
